task: Web App to Mobile Build Blueprint and Backlog

overall_task_success.commentary: The blueprint content is thorough and the process ran fast and unattended, but the deliverable ships with a real duplicate ticket sitting next to an untouched existing one covering the same phase, a direct miss on the task's own rule against creating duplicate issues rather than a stylistic nit. The attachment format also doesn't match what was asked for, one merged file per issue instead of individual relevant tabs. I'd need to reconcile two overlapping foundation tickets myself before the backlog is usable, and I'd also need to split the merged attachments back into the individual tab files the brief actually asked for, a real cleanup cost on top of otherwise solid analysis.

task_accuracy.commentary: When I check it, the blueprint is thorough, the tab structure is complete, the commit is pinned and stated, and the ticket descriptions carry specific, concrete technical detail rather than vague scope language. The real problem sits upstream of the content, the fixture had an open Jira issue covering foundation and authentication work, and this run never checked for it before creating a new ticket under different wording. The result is a fresh ticket sitting alongside an untouched one that covers the same phase, exactly what the task's rule against creating duplicate issues exists to prevent. Strong analytical content sitting on top of a real duplication problem is why this lands well below the middle for me.

efficiency.wrong_actions_recovery: none stated beyond the expected Chrome fallback for Jira attachments, needed because the standard connector doesn't expose a way to upload attachments directly
efficiency.commentary: 25 minutes for a full architecture read, a document with nine tabs, four tickets with attachments, and a Teams post strikes me as a tight runtime for this scope, and when I check the log against what shipped, the run reads as one continuous pass with real visual verification built in rather than skipped. The one small thing I'd flag is that the image review happens across five separate batches, three images, then six, six, five, and five, rather than one consolidated pass, a minor structural inefficiency even though every batch does get checked before the run calls itself done.

writing_quality.commentary: The ticket descriptions are genuinely well structured, an objective, a sprint span, a scoped bullet list, dependencies, and a concrete done checklist on every one, and the Teams message is short and states exactly what changed. Two things hold this back for me. Bundling every relevant tab into one combined PDF per ticket is readable, but it means I have to page through a merged document to find the section that actually matters to that phase, rather than opening the one file that's relevant. And the blueprint's own prose packs long bracketed citation lists directly into the middle of sentences, great for tracing a claim but breaking up the reading flow badly enough that the narrative gets hard to follow.

instruction_following.commentary: When I check it line by line, the tab structure, the commit pin, the cap of four issues, keeping status in To Do only, and the rule to reference secrets rather than copy them are all followed correctly. Two requirements are not. The task is specific that running it again should match issues by exact summary and update in place rather than create something close to a duplicate, and this run creates a new ticket under different wording without checking for the match that was sitting there. And the task asks for the relevant tabs attached to each issue as files, plural, and what shipped is one merged file per issue instead of the individual tab files the instruction describes.

collaboration_autonomy_verification.steering_needed: none, the run completed unattended from the access gate through the Teams post
collaboration_autonomy_verification.additional_editing: I'd want the existing foundation and authentication issue reconciled with the new one this run created before either goes anywhere near a sprint board
collaboration_autonomy_verification.commentary: This ran the whole pipeline without needing me to step in, and the repeated image review during document creation shows real attention to the artifact's actual appearance rather than just confirming writes landed. Where checking its own work falls short is the one place it mattered most, the requirement to match against an existing issue, nothing in the run verifies whether a matching issue already existed before a new one got created, and that gap is exactly what produced the duplicate. Checking that the Jira write succeeded is not the same as checking that it was the right write to make.

citation_quality.commentary: When I check the tickets and the blueprint against the source, almost every claim carries a file and line citation across the whole document, the architecture, the data model, the screen inventory, and the delivery plan all point to exact file locations I can go open myself, well beyond just the Secrets tab. The pricing and licensing figures in the Mobile Stack tab also trace to a named published source list rather than a rounded guess. The one place this thins out is the summary table, it restates the same costs and decisions without repeating a citation per row, so I have to flip back to the prose above to find the source for one line.

gui_action_correctness.commentary: I can see real, demonstrated visual verification here, the run exported and reviewed the rendered attachment PDFs multiple times across several batches of images before calling them finished, a genuine check rather than an assumption. The one gap for me is that this visual pass is narrated in detail for the derived Jira attachment PDFs specifically, but not once for the canonical Google Doc itself, so the document that's actually the source of truth never gets the same on screen confirmation the exported copies do, which is the one place I'd still want to see checked before I'd trust it.
